summary: Missions to the lunar South Pole face extreme lighting and communication constraints: the Moon's 1.54° axial tilt makes the Sun skim the horizon at grazing angles, casting multi-kilometer crater shadows while Earth traces a ±6.69° latitudinal / ±7.90° longitudinal libration loop. Existing tools (JPL Horizons, LROC QuickMap, Moon Trek) require fragmented manual workflows that slow down rapid decisions when a launch slips. LUNAR-NAV is an interactive 3D WebGL and Python/Kaggle mission-operations suite integrating NASA LOLA Digital Elevation Models and JPL Horizons DE440 ephemerides. It empowers mission planners, educators, and the public to compare 11 Artemis, CLPS (IM-1 Odysseus, IM-2 Athena), and international (ISRO Chandrayaan-3 Shiv Shakti Point) sites plus custom coordinates across Primary and Backup Touchdown Dates—simulating 360° vacuum horizons, vertical solar masts, 60 kWh battery survival, 384,400 km DSN RF diffraction links, 500-shot Monte Carlo landing dispersion, and A* PSR rover paths.
details: WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS: 1. Interactive 3D LOLA DEM Digital Twin & Polar Cap Globe (Three.js r128): Renders contour-shaded South Pole topography, grazing solar shadow maps, adjustable telescopic bifacial solar masts (1–30 m) with vacuum horizon dip θ = -√(2h/R_Moon), and double-click lander relocation. 2. Curated NASA/CLPS/ISRO Regions & Custom Coordinate Comparator: Side-by-side trade-off analysis across 11 landmark sites (Connecting Ridge, Shackleton Rim, Mons Mouton, Malapert Massif, Nobile Rim 1 & 2, de Gerlache Rim 2, Haworth Crater PSR, IM-2 Athena March 2025 Forensic Site at 84.79°S 29.20°E, IM-1 Odysseus at 80.13°S 1.44°E, and ISRO Chandrayaan-3 Statio Shiv Shakti at 69.37°S 32.32°E) plus any custom coordinate. 3. Explicit Calendar Date & Launch-Slip Pivot Matrix: Converts UTC dates to Julian Dates (JD) and seasonal solar declinations (±1.5424°), auditing 6 NASA CASSA/TOPSIS GO/NO-GO constraints across Primary vs. Backup dates (+3d, +7d, +10d, +14d slips). 4. Multi-Physics Survival Lab: 500-shot Gaussian Monte Carlo 3σ touchdown dispersion simulator (predicting tip-over & crater shadow risk), A* geodesic rover pathfinder to <110 K Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) water-ice cold traps, and a 384,400 km ITU-R P.526 Fresnel knife-edge diffraction link budget calculator for NASA's 3 DSN complexes (Goldstone, Madrid, Canberra). 5. 3-Tier Audience Mode & 108-Question Socratic Study Notebook: Tailors telemetry for Mission Planners, Classroom Educators, and Public Explorers with a 6-chapter animated physics course and 108 interactive 3D flashcards. TOOLS & LANGUAGES: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js (r128 WebGL), Chart.js, Web Speech & Audio APIs, Python 3 (NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Pillow). SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) ACKNOWLEDGMENT: Code structure, 3D WebGL UI components, browser-synthesized Web Speech audio, and Socratic flashcard text were developed with Super Intelligence (SI / Google Gemini) assistance and embedded with HTML metadata and footer disclosures. No NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers are generated or modified. All orbital mechanics equations and selenographic coordinates were validated against official NASA JPL Horizons DE440 and LRO LOLA data.
